title: The ABA problem
sub: Compare-and-swap checks that a pointer is the same, not that nothing changed.

frames.caption: A lock-free stack: head → A → B. Thread 1 starts a pop. It reads head = A and A.next = B, planning to CAS head from A to B. Then it is preempted.
While thread 1 sleeps, thread 2 pops A, then pops B, and frees both.
Thread 2 pushes a new value. The allocator hands back the memory A used to occupy: a brand-new node, at the same address. The stack is now just head → A (value 99). B is still freed.

Thread 1 wakes up and runs CAS(head, A, B). The head does hold address A, so the CAS succeeds, and head now points at B: freed memory. The new node with value 99 has vanished from the stack, and the next pop reads garbage. Same address, different node: that is ABA.
A lock-free stack: head → A → B. Thread 1 starts a pop. It reads head = A (tag 7) and A.next = B, planning to CAS head from A to B. Then it is preempted.
While thread 1 sleeps, thread 2 pops A, then pops B, and frees both.
Thread 2 pushes a new value. The allocator hands back the memory A used to occupy: a brand-new node, at the same address. The stack is now just head → A (value 99). B is still freed.

Thread 1 runs CAS(head, A + tag 7, B + tag 8). The address matches, but the tag is now 10, because every successful CAS bumped it. The CAS fails, thread 1 rereads head, and retries correctly. The tag turns 'same address' into 'same address and nothing has happened since'. (Thread 1 must also not touch freed node A: tagging fixes ABA, but reclamation still needs hazard pointers or epochs.)
